[id="disallowed-model-error-messages_{context}"]
= Disallowed model error messages

[role='_abstract']
When a model has been disallow-listed by an administrator, non-administrator users see specific behaviors depending on how they try to access the model.
Understanding these behaviors helps you distinguish between intentional governance restrictions and system errors, so that you can take the correct action.

[id="model-visibility-behavior_{context}"]
== Model visibility behavior

The following table describes how disallow-listed models appear to non-administrator users.

.Disallowed model visibility behavior
[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Access method
|Behavior

|Browsing the catalog
|The disallow-listed model does not appear in the catalog.
It is hidden from search results, category listings, and filter results.
Non-administrator users have no indication that the model exists.

|Direct link to the model details page
|The message "Model is disabled by your administrator" is displayed instead of the model details.

|API query for the model
|The API response indicates that the model is disabled by an administrator.
|===

[id="understanding-the-error-message_{context}"]
== Understanding the error message

The "Model is disabled by your administrator" message indicates that an {productname-short} administrator or cluster administrator has intentionally restricted access to this model.
This is a governance control, not a system error or a temporary outage.

Common reasons for disallow-listing a model include:

* Compliance with organizational security policies
* Regulatory restrictions on specific model types or providers
* Intellectual property concerns
* Internal approval processes that have not yet been completed

[id="impact-on-deployed-models_{context}"]
== Impact on deployed models

Governance restrictions apply only to the model catalog.
If you have already deployed a model that is later disallow-listed, your existing deployment continues to function normally.
Disallow-listing does not stop, remove, or change running model instances.

[id="resolving-access-issues_{context}"]
== Resolving access issues

If you need access to a disallow-listed model, contact your {productname-short} administrator or cluster administrator.
Provide the name of the model and the reason that you need access so that the administrator can evaluate your request against the organization's governance policies.

Do not file a support case for disallow-listed models.
The restriction is an intentional administrative action, not a product defect.
